steps: A coordinator grants A ownership until bounded expiry T.

lesson.scenario: A metadata worker holds a renewable 10-second lease to compact one shard.
entities: Atomically records owner, expiry, and generation

steps.title: Lease absent
steps.narration: Shard 7 has no current owner at 10:00:00.
steps.outcome: Either worker may attempt an atomic acquisition.
steps.invariant: The lease record must be changed conditionally.

steps.title: A acquires
steps.outcome: A may compact within the bounded lease interval.
steps.invariant: The holder must stop before expiry minus the safety margin.

steps.title: A renews
steps.narration: A renews before the safety margin and keeps generation 34.
steps.outcome: Authority is extended without changing owners.
steps.invariant: Renewal succeeds only if owner and generation still match.

steps.title: Lease expires
steps.narration: A pauses beyond expiry and must consider its authority lost.
steps.outcome: Time bounds permit a new owner to contend.
steps.invariant: An expired holder cannot infer continued ownership from local memory.

steps.title: B acquires next generation
steps.narration: B atomically replaces the expired record with generation 35.
steps.outcome: B is the new lease holder.
steps.invariant: Leases should be paired with fencing because A may resume and attempt stale side effects.

production.scenario: A supplier-catalog sync service grants a short lease per supplier account so only one pod polls a flaky supplier API and writes prices into the retail catalog at a time.
components: Starts refreshes for supplier account 44 every five minutes
Polls supplier 44 while it still owns the lease
Waits to take over supplier 44 if pod A stops renewing
Authoritative owner, expiry, and generation for supplier 44
Source of truth for new SKUs and price changes
Authoritative imported supplier rows for the storefront
Expires stale owners and alerts on repeated takeover
flows: The scheduler asks pod A to begin the next pull cycle for supplier 44.
Pod A must first become the recorded owner before it talks to the supplier API.
pull delta feed while lease generation 118 is valid
Only the leased pod fetches the new catalog delta so the supplier is not double-polled.
The imported rows land in the retail catalog as the new authoritative storefront copy for supplier 44.
During a long sync, pod A keeps extending the lease so no standby pod starts a second import.
If pod A stops heartbeating, the monitor marks generation 118 dead once the lease timeout passes.
Pod B can safely resume pulling deltas only after the old lease is expired and a new generation is recorded.
